clue.text: Piano virtuoso's record on radio

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: words heard on the radio are spoken, so this signals a soundalike

parts.note: a record can be a list, a written register of items

explanation.surface: A broadcaster plays a famous pianist's recording on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': 'Piano virtuoso is record on radio'. LIST spoken aloud sounds like the composer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the most celebrated concert pianist of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Cosmetic the county set originally applied to cheek

indicators.note: applied to means the county and the first letter are attached after the word for cheek

parts.note: lip is impudence, cheek
Glos is the abbreviation for Gloucestershire, an English county

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of set is taken

explanation.surface: The county set dabbed some make-up on their cheeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheek' suggests a face, which fits the make-up, but means impudence. GLOS is Gloucestershire, a county in western England; 'originally' takes S from 'set'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip gloss is a shiny make-up applied to the mouth.

clue.text: Leaks in port side of boat at sea make it this

definitions.text: Leaks in port side of boat at sea make it this

indicators.note: at sea means the letters are thrown into confusion and must be rearranged
port is the left side, so the leftmost letter of boat is taken

explanation.surface: Holes in the left side of a vessel will send it to the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges LEAKSIN plus B. The whole clue is also the definition: leaks make a boat liable to go down.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that can be holed and go down is one capable of sinking.

clue.text: Book holiday for number of chaps after a row?

definitions.text: Book holiday for number of chaps after a row?

parts.words: Book holiday for number of chaps after a row?
parts.note: a comic novel of a boating holiday on the Thames, also how one might describe a trio of men sitting in their craft after rowing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Book holiday' looks like making a reservation; it is a book about a holiday. The 1889 comic novel by Jerome K Jerome follows three friends rowing up the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome K Jerome's novel describes a trio of friends taking a rowing trip up the river.

clue.text: Spot of trouble about tour is breaking hearts, say

indicators.note: about means the word for the trouble is turned round

parts.note: being in a jam is being in a spot of trouble

indicators.note: breaking up the words tour and is lets their letters be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some bother on a concert tour is breaking the hearts of fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns JAM into MAJ; 'breaking' rearranges TOUR IS into ORSUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, hearts and spades are the major suits, scoring more than clubs and diamonds.

clue.text: Recall lines overlooked in short note

indicators.note: overlooked means the letters for lines are left out

parts.note: memory is the power of recall
RY is short for railway, railway lines

explanation.surface: In a brief note, a reminder ignored some lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooked' removes RY (railway) from MEMORY.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo, short for memorandum, is a brief written message.

clue.text: Hare krishna's first to appear before religious leader in a court, with superior judge

indicators.note: superior means placed above, at the top of this down entry
in means the letter and leader sit inside the a and court letters
before means that letter comes ahead of the religious leader
the first letter of krishna's is the one taken

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

explanation.surface: A Hare Krishna devotee and a rabbi appear in court before a senior judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hare krishna' reads as a sect; 'Hare' alone is the definition. 'in' sets the K and leader inside A and the court; 'superior' puts the judge on top in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackrabbit is a large long-eared North American hare.

clue.text: Test cricket is no diversion for boffin

indicators.note: a diversion sends things off in new directions, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist finds five-day cricket no fun to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diversion' looks like entertainment; it rearranges TESTCRICKETISNO. A Test is a full international cricket match lasting up to five days.
explanation.definitionFit: A boffin is a British colloquial word for a scientist or technical expert, someone of great intellect.

clue.text: There's agreement to raise son in more than one marriage

indicators.note: to raise means the letter for son is lifted higher up in this down entry

parts.note: marriages are unions

explanation.surface: Parents agree to bring up a son across several marriages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise son' suggests parenting; here 'to raise' moves S up from the bottom of UNIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in unison is to act together in complete accord.

clue.text: Essay without conclusion's given in

indicators.note: without means outside, so the word for essay goes around the other

parts.note: to essay is to attempt, try
the conclusion of something is its end

explanation.surface: An essay with no ending is handed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but here means outside, an old sense; 'in' as a definition means fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is in is currently fashionable.

clue.text: Comprehensive in flap involving old beak

indicators.note: involving means the word for flap wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: to be in a flap is to be in a panic
a ram is the beak-like projection on a warship's bow

explanation.surface: Someone in a flutter over an elderly magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beak' is British slang for a magistrate, which the surface suggests; here it is the ram on an old warship's bow. 'involving' wraps the flap word around the old and beak letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoramic view takes in the whole scene, so it is all-embracing.

clue.text: Murder, perhaps, of most characters in old Soviet republic

indicators.note: taking most of the characters in the name means dropping its final letter

parts.note: Crimea was an autonomous republic within the Soviet Union

explanation.surface: A killing committed in a former Soviet region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most characters in' drops the last A from CRIMEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Murder is an example of an offence against the law.

clue.text: Rolling drunk

explanation.surface: Staggering about after too much to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rolling in money is wealthy, and someone tanked up on drink is intoxicated: both senses fit the one word.

clue.text: Purchase previously vacant property one can dispose of at will

definitions.text: property one can dispose of at will

indicators.note: previously means the word for vacant comes before the word for purchase

parts.note: vacant means free, unoccupied
a purchase is a grip or hold

explanation.surface: Buying an empty building that the owner may sell whenever they like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' looks like buying but means a grip, HOLD; 'previously' puts FREE first.
explanation.definitionFit: Freehold tenure gives outright ownership with no time limit, unlike a lease.

clue.text: What shop has to sell, yet is not moving at all

parts.note: a shop's stock is the goods it has for sale
still and yet both mean nevertheless

explanation.surface: A shop with goods to sell is not doing any business.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still means completely motionless.

clue.text: Glue-sniffing and crack forbidden in most quarters

parts.note: to crack a problem is to solve it

indicators.note: in means the word for forbidden sits within the compass letters

parts.note: three of the four compass quarters: north, south, east
tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, forbidden

explanation.surface: Inhaling glue and taking drugs are banned almost everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' suggests the drug but means solve. 'in' sets the forbidden word among three of the four compass points; tabu is an accepted spelling of taboo.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue-sniffing is the misuse of the fumes of household solvents to get high.

clue.text: This may provide well-known person with a boost

definitions.text: This may provide well-known person with a boost

parts.note: a face is a celebrity, a well-known figure
a lift is a boost

explanation.surface: Cosmetic surgery can give a celebrity a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the operation, which a famous face may seek.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic surgery that tightens the skin raises sagging features.

clue.text: German rebel, disguised, hiding in Russian capital

indicators.note: hiding means the rearranged letters conceal the small word inside them
disguised means the letters of rebel appear in altered order
capital means the first, capital letter of Russian

explanation.surface: A German insurgent in disguise lies low in Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' rearranges the rebel letters as BERLE; 'hiding' tucks the little word in among them; 'capital' takes the first letter of Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: A Berliner is a native or inhabitant of Germany's capital city.

clue.text: I'm certain Democrat is wrong to show bias

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are put in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A partisan claims a Democratic politician's stance is mistaken and slanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges IMCERTAIN, D and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To discriminate is to treat people unfairly, favouring some over others.

clue.text: Book in which goon appears

explanation.surface: A book featuring a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccles is the abbreviation of Ecclesiastes, a book of the Old Testament, and the dim-witted Eccles was a character in The Goon Show, the 1950s BBC radio comedy.

clue.text: Fall in gym after taking breather

indicators.note: taking means the letters for gym take in the breather

parts.note: PE (physical education) is school gym
a lung is a breathing organ

explanation.surface: Someone collapses in the gym after stopping for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' suggests a pause; it is a breathing organ. 'taking' puts it inside the gym letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge is to drop suddenly downwards.

clue.text: Cave in ridge between mountains found by mistake

indicators.note: found by means the col is placed beside the word for mistake

parts.note: a col is a saddle or pass between two peaks
a lapse is a slip or error

explanation.surface: A mountain pass discovered by accident leads into a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' looks like a noun; here 'Cave in' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: When a roof caves in it falls down, which is a structural failure.

clue.text: A slippery creature, we hear, shows temper

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is to be taken as spoken

parts.note: an eel is a proverbially slippery fish

explanation.surface: An eel displays a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' looks like anger; here it is the verb, toughening metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To anneal metal or glass is to heat it and cool it slowly to toughen it, as smiths do.

clue.text: Period out east for speculator wanting quick profit

indicators.note: out means the letter for east is taken away

parts.note: a stage is a period or phase

explanation.surface: A trader eager to cash in fast spends time in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E from STAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag buys new shares hoping to sell them at once at a profit.

clue.text: Equivalent of releasing slowly?

indicators.note: releasing means letting a run of letters out of the words Equivalent of

explanation.surface: Something that amounts to letting go at a gentle pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Equivalent of' looks like part of a definition, but it is the text holding the answer; 'releasing' lets it out. The question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is the Italian musical direction to play at a slow pace.

clue.text: Hunch one needs batting lessons

parts.note: a batsman batting in cricket is said to be in
tuition is teaching or lessons

explanation.surface: A gut feeling that one needs coaching at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: IN is the cricket term for the side or player currently batting.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunch is a feeling arrived at without reasoning, which is instinctive knowledge.

clue.text: Plant — kind to wilt?

parts.note: a kind person is sweet
to flag is to droop or tire

explanation.surface: A gentle plant inclined to droop?
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet flag is an aromatic reed-like marsh plant, Acorus calamus.

clue.text: Murphy is one who tries but hasn't succeeded

definitions.note: murphy is Irish-derived slang for a potato

indicators.note: hasn't means the letter for succeeded is missing from the word

parts.note: a taster tries food or drink
s is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: Murphy keeps trying but never manages it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murphy' looks like a surname; it is slang for a potato. 'hasn't' drops S from TASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tater is a colloquial potato, and murphy is another nickname for that vegetable.
